correctness.rationale: For a hypothetical isometry \(T:\mathbb C^3\to M_2(\mathbb C)\), the exact \(2\times2\) identity \(\|A\|_4^4=\|A\|_2^4-2|\det A|^2\) gives \(2|q(x)|^2=(x^*Hx)^2-\|x\|_2^4\). Positivity forces \(H\ge I\), and unitary diagonalization makes the right side invariant under independent coordinate phases. A nonzero homogeneous holomorphic quadratic with torus-invariant modulus must be one monomial; coefficient comparison then forces all eigenvalues of \(H\) to one and simultaneously forces that monomial coefficient to vanish. Thus \(q=0\) and every matrix in the three-dimensional image is singular. A direct determinant-polynomial argument shows a complex linear subspace of \(M_2\) consisting entirely of singular matrices has dimension at most two, contradiction. First-row embeddings give the matching Hilbert plane in \(S_4^2\) and \(\ell_2^3\) in \(S_4^3\). The proof is exact and uses no numerical inference.
